customer-jane: Hey — running into partial JSON in streaming responses from /v1/streams. The stream often ends mid-object (missing trailing } or value trimmed). ~5% of requests, typically after ~18–25s. Sharing a minimal curl and the tail hex.

olivia: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact curl -v you used and a hex dump of the truncated tail? Also which SDK + any proxy in front?

customer-jane: curl I used:
```
curl -i -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \
  https://api.redwood.dev/v1/streams -d @req.json
```
Tail (hexdump) we captured (last 48 bytes):
```
00000030  7b 22 74 79 70 65 22 3a  22 72 65 73 70 6f 6e 73 7b  |{"type":"respons{|
00000040  22 64 61 74 61 22 3a 22 7b  5c 22 74 65 78 74 5c 22  |"data":"{\\"text\\"|
00000050  3a 22 68 65 6c 6c 6f 20 77  6f 72 6c 64 22 2c 20     |:"hello world", |
00000060  22 70 61 72 74 69 61 6c  22 3a 22 74 72 75 6e 63     |"partial":"trunc|
00000070  61 74 65 64 22 0a                                   |ated".        |
```
Note: response ends abruptly, next chunk missing.

ashley: Got it, thanks for the dump. From that hex it looks like stream closed mid-chunk (we're seeing a partial JSON object). @kevin any early theories? :eyes:

kevin: Most likely a midstream FIN from a proxy/edge (Cloudflare or nginx) cutting the connection between keepalives. Two quick repros I use:
1) `curl --no-buffer` with artificially slow consumer (sleep per-byte)
2) Node fetch example that reproduces with flaky proxy:
```
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${KEY}` } });
  res.body.on('data', chunk => { /* slow parse + sleep to simulate client slowness */ });
})();
```
If you can run the curl + this node snippet against your proxy we can see if the proxy emits an upstream close.

tara: If you have nginx between client and our edge, check these settings on the proxy: `proxy_read_timeout 120s; proxy_send_timeout 120s; proxy_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` Also confirm no intermediate load balancer has a shorter idle timeout.

kevin: Server-side mitigations we recommend: send a small heartbeat/comment every 8–12s for SSE (`:hb\n\n`), and for structured/json mode emit an explicit sentinel early on and at the end (e.g. `data: {\"_sentinel\":\"start\"}\n\n` and final `data: {\"_sentinel\":\"end\"}\n\n`). That way clients can detect midstream closes and attempt rejoin/retry.

customer-jane: We added heartbeat => reduced frequency but still seeing truncation in a couple traces. Proxy logs show: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` from our nginx in front of the edge.

olivia: Copying infra. @tara @kevin — customer can share full proxy logs/pcap. For immediate mitigation we can offer two options: 1) switch to non-streaming responses (set `stream=false`) or 2) enable the SDK's streaming-stitch fallback (it will attempt to re-open and resume from last known token). Which would you prefer?

customer-jane: Please send the SDK workaround steps for now — want to avoid user-facing 5xxs during business hours.

ashley: SDK workaround (quick):
1) If you control client, set `stream=false` to fall back to a single response.
2) If you need streaming: enable `auto_stitch=true` in the SDK (or implement client stitch): keep the last ~256 chars of the current incomplete buffer; on JSON parse failure, open a new stream with a small `resume_from` token marker (our SDK exposes `resume_from_last_token`).
Example pseudo: `if (parseFail) reopenStream({ resume_from: lastTokenId })`

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1432 — eng-runtime investigating. Assigned: kevin.

kevin: I'll investigate edge idle windows + upstream close behavior and push a runtime update to emit an extra flush at ~5s after every N tokens. Will post updates here. Thanks, everyone.
